summary:
Small source-only research product closing the last wholly unread public surface; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

What was closed: observer.go (source S66, lines 58-140) carries no protocol responsibility. Raft emits Observations only from paths that already produced the state; the emit path takes a read lock and, for a non-blocking observer, discards rather than blocking the protocol (drops are counted), while the blocking behaviour is documented on both NewObserver and observe — so the delivery policy is a caller contract rather than a library duty. The corresponding Surface therefore moves from deferred to externalized with its reason and source updated; no behavior, fact, requirement or other object changes, so the four confirmed findings and every accepted result keep their basis.

Product contents: the draft map (base version 15) with that one Surface disposition change; feedback recording the closure and the frontier.

Ledger and frontier now explicit: the in-memory snapshot store is the last unread file (net_transport's stream/connection handling and the fuzzy/bench helpers have been skimmed only). Four confirmed in-scope violations stand — batching-FSM ConfigurationStore delivery, heartbeat fast-path header gate (with measured vote-suppression consequence), TimeoutNow sender attribution (with measured vote-granting consequence), and snapshot install log-tail alignment — each keeping an open deployment premise: reachability of an out-of-window heartbeat sender, reachability of an unconfigured TimeoutNow sender, whether batching FSMs are exempt from ConfigurationStore, and how long a snapshot-installed tail persists under a live leader. Leads with no obligation remain: ReloadConfig notification scope, the processHeartbeat concurrency contract, and the transport TimeoutScale configuration discrepancy.
